newsitem.title: INDONESIA: World Bank says Bukaka report mistaken.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says Bukaka report mistaken.

text.p: The Indonesian office of the World Bank has denied a newspaper report that it had given projects worth hundreds of millions of dollars to local engineering firm PT Bukaka Teknik Utama.

"It's a bit mistaken. The World Bank does not give anybody projects. We lend money to the governments and the governments select the firms that undertake the projects. We do not select the firms," Dennis de Tray, director of the World Bank's resident staff in Indonesia, told Reuters.
Brokers said Bukaka shares rose 325 rupiah, or 21.31 percent, to 1,850 rupiah in active late trading on Wednesday due to the newspaper report.

Bisnis Indonesia newspaper on Wednesday quoted Bukaka's president director Fadel Muhammad as saying the bank had offered the company some power transmissions, airport infrastructure and railway projects in several Asian countries.
De Tray on Wednesday also denied that the bank had recommended that Bukaka undertake the projects, saying it was up to the respective governments to make the decisions.
"(The World Bank) does not recommend one company over another nor do we pre-approve companies. Those activities are left to the governments that actually manage the projects," he said.
"The World Bank is encouraging companies in developing countries who have sophisticated products to penetrate other developing countries," Muhammad was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
He said the projects were in Cambodia, Laos, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and India with a total investment of hundreds of millions of dollars.
Bukaka officials were not immediately available for comment.
